name: Tessera Industries Micro-Hologram Projector MHP-3
description: A pocket-sized holographic projector that creates a 30 cm cube of volumetric imagery, sufficient for displaying 3D maps, schematics, faces, or small-scale tactical models. The MHP-3 is a personal information display device that replaces flat screens with true 3D visualization, interfacing with neural implants for direct data input. Users project building blueprints, rotate 3D models of equipment, display facial identification holos, and visualize tactical situations in miniature. The device has become standard professional equipment for engineers, investigators, and tactical planners.

specifications.input: Neural interface or wireless data connection

story_hooks: An MHP-3 found at a crime scene was still projecting when investigators arrived — it displayed a 3D map of the building with entry and exit routes marked, a complete tactical plan left behind by the perpetrators.
MHP-3 projectors have been hacked to display subliminal images within their normal holographic output — users are seeing content they did not request, embedded in their legitimate projections.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist rectangular solid resembling a premium cigarette case or small jewelry box. The device has a subtly curved top surface with a faint luminescent seam running its perimeter. Its form factor suggests precision engineering—almost jewel-like in its compactness. The front face features a dark optical lens window slightly recessed beneath the main housing.
physical_description.dimensions: 8.5 cm × 5.2 cm × 2.1 cm (matchbox-sized, fits easily in a palm or shirt pocket)
physical_description.weight_description: 50 grams—light enough to be pocketable, feels substantial but never burdensome. Easily held one-handed during operation.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum alloy chassis with biocompatible polymer accent panels
physical_description.finish: Brushed gunmetal with a soft matte coating; the top surface has a subtle iridescent oil-slick shimmer visible under direct light, hinting at the holographic technology within
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary body with accent strips of deep teal/cyan running along the edges. The optical lens window is black with a faint blue glow when active.
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimal visible UI: a small pressure-sensitive touch pad on the right edge (roughly 1.5 cm × 0.5 cm), a barely-visible status LED trio (green/amber/red) above the lens, and a micro USB-C port recessed on the bottom edge. No physical buttons. Neural interface connection manifests as a thin metallic contact pad on the back.
distinctive_features: Holographic lens window with concentric circular micro-optics visible under magnification
Soft cyan glow emanating from the seam when powered on
The top surface subtly rises in the center, suggesting internal optical projection mechanisms
Hairline etching along the edges marking gesture control zones for neural input
A barely-visible Φ symbol (QUANTA branding) laser-etched into the bottom corner
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo (a geometric tessellating pattern) printed on the rear; 'MHP-3' and 'Vasquez Biocompatible Materials' stamped discretely on the underside; regulatory compliance marks (GLMZ approved, neural-safe certification) in micro-print
physical_description.condition_typical: Clean, pristine surface finish on new units; well-used examples show minor fingerprint smudging on the lens window and slight wear to the touch pad. The iridescent shimmer becomes more pronounced with age/use. No visible degradation—these are built to last.

image_prompt: Product photography: Tessera Industries MHP-3 micro-hologram projector displayed on a dark brushed steel workbench, angled at 45 degrees. Dramatic side-lighting from a single neon teal source emphasizes the device's metallic edges and the iridescence of its top surface. In soft focus background: neural interface cables, scattered datapads, and a chrome cybernetic hand reaching toward the holographic display.
